entries.title: Enable virtualization-based security (VBS)
entries.description: Turns on the hypervisor-backed secure environment (Secure Boot required) that isolates security features such as memory integrity and Credential Guard from the normal OS. Does not set the UEFI lock, so it can be reverted.
entries.rationale: VBS is the foundation the Microsoft baseline and STIG build credential and code-integrity protection on. New Windows 11 22H2+ installs enable it on capable hardware; upgraded machines often lack it.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\System\Device Guard\Turn On Virtualization Based Security

sideEffects: Small performance cost, worse on older CPUs that lack MBEC/GMET hardware acceleration.
Impairs older VirtualBox/VMware nested-virtualization paths and some anti-cheat or kernel drivers.
Requiring platform security with DMA protection (value 3) silently disables VBS on machines without an IOMMU.

entries.title: Enable memory integrity (HVCI)
entries.description: Turns on hypervisor-enforced code integrity (Core isolation > Memory integrity), which checks that kernel-mode code is signed and unmodified before it runs. Does not set the UEFI lock.
entries.rationale: HVCI blocks a large class of kernel exploits and unsigned driver attacks; it is part of the Microsoft baseline and STIG. Needs VBS running underneath it.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\System\Device Guard\Turn On Virtualization Based Security

sideEffects: Unsigned or outdated drivers block enablement or cause a bugcheck; Windows lists the offending driver in the UI.
Recovery from a boot failure may require a WinRE registry edit; a UEFI-locked variant needs Secure Boot disabled to recover.

entries.title: Enable kernel-mode hardware-enforced stack protection
entries.description: Turns on CET shadow stacks for kernel-mode code so return addresses cannot be silently overwritten by exploits. Requires memory integrity (HVCI) running and a CET-capable CPU.
entries.rationale: Shadow stacks defeat a common ROP-style kernel exploitation technique. Windows enables it by default on new installs with capable hardware; there is no Group Policy surface, so it is set through the registry key the Windows Security toggle writes.
sideEffects: Incompatible kernel drivers (older anti-cheat, some AV, virtual device drivers) can cause a bugcheck or make the feature refuse to enable; Windows Security shows the blocking driver.

entries.title: Enable Credential Guard (no UEFI lock)
entries.description: Runs the LSA credential store inside the VBS-isolated environment (LSAIso) so domain and cached secrets cannot be read or replayed from LSASS. Uses the value that does not set a firmware lock, so it can be reverted. Enterprise and Education only.
entries.rationale: Credential Guard is the primary defence against pass-the-hash and pass-the-ticket credential theft (Microsoft baseline, STIG CAT I, ACSC high priority). It requires VBS and Secure Boot and is only licensed on Enterprise/Education.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\System\Device Guard\Turn On Virtualization Based Security\Credential Guard Configuration

sideEffects: Breaks Kerberos DES and unconstrained delegation, TGT extraction, and NTLMv1 (removed in 24H2 regardless).
MS-CHAPv2 with saved domain credentials (PEAP-MSCHAPv2 Wi-Fi/VPN) prompts every time or fails; CredSSP credential delegation and third-party SSO that hooks LSA can break.
Not supported on Exchange servers and offers no benefit on domain controllers.

entries.title: Enable Credential Guard with UEFI lock
entries.description: Enables Credential Guard and persists the setting in a UEFI variable so it cannot be turned off remotely by simply clearing the registry. Enterprise and Education only. Disabling it later requires firmware access.
entries.rationale: The UEFI-locked variant is the Microsoft baseline recommendation for high-assurance devices because malware or a rushed rollback cannot silently disable credential isolation. It requires VBS and Secure Boot and is only licensed on Enterprise/Education.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\System\Device Guard\Turn On Virtualization Based Security\Credential Guard Configuration

sideEffects: All of the Credential Guard breakage (NTLMv1, Kerberos DES, unconstrained delegation, MS-CHAPv2 saved credentials, CredSSP, LSA-hooking SSO).
The UEFI lock requires firmware access and the LSA opt-out tool to disable Credential Guard later.

entries.title: Disable WDigest clear-text credential caching
entries.description: Sets UseLogonCredential to 0 so the legacy WDigest provider does not keep clear-text passwords in LSASS memory. This is the safe default on Windows 8.1 and later, pinned explicitly.
entries.rationale: When WDigest caches plain-text credentials, a memory dump of LSASS yields passwords directly (a favourite of Mimikatz). Disabled by default on Windows 11; setting 0 keeps it that way even if something re-enables it.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\MS Security Guide\WDigest Authentication (disabling may require KB2871997)

entries.title: Block custom SSPs and APs from loading into LSASS
entries.description: Sets AllowCustomSSPsAPs to 0 so third-party security support providers and authentication packages cannot load into the LSA process.
entries.rationale: Custom SSPs/APs are a classic credential-theft persistence mechanism; the Microsoft 22H2 baseline disables them. Legitimate third-party providers are rare on standalone Windows 11.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\System\Local Security Authority\Allow Custom SSPs and APs to be loaded into LSASS

sideEffects: Third-party security support providers and authentication packages (some SSO, smart-card middleware, legacy AV) fail to load.

entries.title: Set LAN Manager authentication level to NTLMv2 only
entries.description: Sets LmCompatibilityLevel to 5 so the machine sends only NTLMv2 and refuses inbound LM and NTLMv1 authentication. Windows 11 defaults to 3 (send NTLMv2 only) but still accepts weaker inbound protocols.
entries.rationale: LM and NTLMv1 are trivially crackable and enable relay attacks; the STIG rates this CAT I. Level 5 additionally refuses weak inbound authentication to the local SMB server and services.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Network security: LAN Manager authentication level

sideEffects: Breaks inbound authentication from very old clients (Windows XP/2003, some ancient NAS or printers) that only speak LM/NTLMv1; outbound authentication is unaffected.

entries.title: Do not store the LAN Manager hash
entries.description: Sets NoLMHash to 1 so Windows never stores the weak LM hash of account passwords. This is the Windows 11 default, pinned explicitly.
entries.rationale: The LM hash is easily cracked; not storing it removes a credential-theft target. The STIG rates it CAT I. Default is already 1.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Network security: Do not store LAN Manager hash value on next password change

entries.title: Require NTLMv2 and 128-bit NTLM session security
entries.description: Sets NTLMMinClientSec and NTLMMinServerSec to 0x20080000 (537395200) so both the NTLM client and server require NTLMv2 session security and 128-bit encryption.
entries.rationale: Without a minimum, NTLM can negotiate down to weak session security; the Microsoft baseline and STIG require NTLMv2 plus 128-bit. Legacy apps that negotiate without these are very rare on Windows 11.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Network security: Minimum session security for NTLM SSP based (including secure RPC) clients

sideEffects: Breaks legacy applications that negotiate NTLM without 128-bit or NTLMv2 session security (very rare on Windows 11).

entries.title: Limit blank-password accounts to console logon
entries.description: Sets LimitBlankPasswordUse to 1 so local accounts with a blank password can only be used at the physical console, never over the network. This is the Windows 11 default, pinned explicitly.
entries.rationale: Prevents a blank-password local account from being used for remote logon; the STIG and CIS require it. Default is already 1.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Accounts: Limit local account use of blank passwords to console logon only

entries.title: Block Microsoft accounts for logon (organisational profiles)
entries.description: Sets NoConnectedUser to 3 and DisableUserAuth to 1 so users cannot add or sign in with a consumer Microsoft account and consumer MSA authentication is blocked. Scoped to Enterprise/Education; never applied on a Home preset.
entries.rationale: Organisations that require domain or Entra identities disable consumer Microsoft accounts to keep credentials and data under management (Microsoft baseline, STIG). On personal PCs this breaks core Microsoft sign-in, so it is limited to managed editions.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Accounts: Block Microsoft accounts

sideEffects: Breaks Microsoft account sign-in, Microsoft Store purchases, Xbox, and personal OneDrive.
Should never be applied on a Home/personal preset; see the privacy documentation cross-reference.

entries.title: Disable PKU2U online-identity authentication
entries.description: Sets AllowOnlineID to 0 so this computer does not accept PKU2U authentication requests that use online identities.
entries.rationale: PKU2U lets unmanaged peer devices authenticate to each other with online identities, which the baseline and STIG disable on managed machines. On Entra-joined or Microsoft-account workgroup PCs this is used for peer RDP/SMB, so it should be reviewed there rather than blindly enforced.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Network security: Allow PKU2U authentication requests to this computer to use online identities

sideEffects: Breaks peer authentication between Entra-joined or Microsoft-account devices (for example RDP or SMB to another Entra-joined PC using Entra credentials).

entries.title: Allow delegation of non-exportable credentials (Remote Credential Guard)
entries.description: Sets AllowProtectedCreds to 1 so this RDP host permits the safer Remote Credential Guard and Restricted Admin delegation modes that never send reusable credentials to the remote session.
entries.rationale: Enabling protected-credential delegation lets RDP sessions avoid exposing passwords on the remote host, mitigating credential theft from compromised servers. No downside on standalone machines.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\System\Credentials Delegation\Remote host allows delegation of non-exportable credentials

entries.title: Harden credential delegation and Encryption Oracle Remediation
entries.description: Sets AllowDefaultCredentials to 0 so default credentials are not delegated, and AllowEncryptionOracle to 0 (Force Updated Clients) so CredSSP refuses to talk to hosts missing the CVE-2018-0886 patch.
entries.rationale: Delegating default credentials and permitting the CredSSP encryption oracle both enable credential theft and man-in-the-middle attacks; the Microsoft baseline sets Encryption Oracle Remediation to Force Updated Clients.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\System\Credentials Delegation\Encryption Oracle Remediation

sideEffects: Encryption Oracle Remediation set to Force Updated Clients blocks CredSSP (for example RDP) to hosts that never received the 2018 CVE-2018-0886 update.

entries.title: Apply UAC token filtering to local accounts over the network
entries.description: Sets LocalAccountTokenFilterPolicy to 0 so local administrator accounts receive a filtered (standard-user) token when logging on over the network. This is the Windows default; value 1 is a pass-the-hash enabler.
entries.rationale: Leaving local admins with a full remote token makes pass-the-hash lateral movement trivial; the Microsoft baseline, STIG and CIS enforce token filtering. Many RMM and home-lab tools set 1, so a value of 1 should be flagged as a finding.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\MS Security Guide\Apply UAC restrictions to local accounts on network logons

sideEffects: Breaks remote administration that relies on a local admin account (PsExec, WinRM, admin$ shares) — common in RMM and home-lab workflows that intentionally set the value to 1.

entries.title: Disable MPR credential notifications to network providers
entries.description: Sets EnableMPR to 0 so the Multiple Provider Router does not forward logon credential notifications to registered network providers.
entries.rationale: MPR notifications let a rogue network provider harvest credentials at logon; the Microsoft 23H2 baseline disables them.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\MS Security Guide\Enable MPR notifications for the system

sideEffects: Third-party network providers that rely on MPR credential notifications (some legacy SSO, password-sync or file-sync clients) stop receiving logon notifications.

entries.title: Do not store passwords for network authentication
entries.description: Sets DisableDomainCreds to 1 so Windows will not save passwords or credentials for network authentication in Credential Manager.
entries.rationale: Stored network credentials can be extracted and replayed; refusing to store them removes that target. This is a high-impact hardening reserved for the strictest profile.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Network access: Do not allow storage of passwords and credentials for network authentication

sideEffects: Breaks Credential Manager for domain and network credentials: saved mapped-drive passwords, saved RDP credentials, and some application SSO; users must re-enter passwords each session.

entries.title: Harden Windows Hello anti-spoofing and PIN length
entries.description: Enables enhanced anti-spoofing for facial recognition (EnhancedAntiSpoofing=1) and sets a minimum Hello PIN length of 6, strengthening the local biometric and PIN sign-in.
entries.rationale: Enhanced anti-spoofing rejects photo-based facial-recognition attacks and a 6-digit minimum PIN resists guessing; both are recommended by the Microsoft baseline, STIG and ACSC. Requiring a TPM (a stricter option) is left out of this baseline entry because it blocks Hello on machines without one.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Biometrics\Facial Features\Configure enhanced anti-spoofing

sideEffects: Enhanced anti-spoofing disables Windows Hello Face on cameras that lack IR/liveness support.
A minimum PIN length of 6 forces users whose PIN is shorter to reset it.
